meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was a zero entered in the gradebook before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What was the basis for it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft elsewhere and paste it in, so what does that prove?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Is anything on his record right now, Hale? Whatever happens here, it stays off it and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Let me read it myself. Students misquote from memory all the time, so why is one bad line more than that?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I'll check the scene tonight. What else do you have?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. Isn't that called revising?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. To put this behind him, I'll accept the rewrite, private, with nothing on his record. I want it in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put Thursday, the time and the room in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday the twelfth after school, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want that commitment in writing, along with the time and the room. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, replacing the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with the time and room, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times, then answered her drafted-elsewhere point by inviting a dated draft you could check, which gave her something she could verify herself.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you real ground, though you moved to the rewrite offer without answering her point that changing an argument between outline and essay is just revising.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay appearing after 11 PM the night before it was due, came close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether changing his argument was just revising, answer that before you offer 4.4, so the rewrite follows from all three pieces standing.
